 NBA Karl-Anthony Towns Brings Team-First Lessons From New Jersey to Knicks Championship Run
 Karl-Anthony Towns helped the New York Knicks win a title in his second season with the club. People who knew him back in New Jersey say lessons from his childhood…
 Autumn Wingate 
 Published Nov 17, 2026 11:04 AM EST Share this story Karl-Anthony Towns helped the New York Knicks win a title in his second season with the club. People who knew him back in New Jersey say lessons from his childhood shaped his role, according to Complex . The Knicks won it all with Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, and Josh Hart. It was the franchise's first championship in 53 years.
 The Knicks fell behind 2-1 to the Atlanta Hawks in the first round. Then head coach Mike Brown started using Towns at the high post. That gave him more chances to drive and pass. New York lost only one more game that postseason, Game 3 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs.
 Game 4 came down to the wire. Anunoby's tip-in put New York up 107-106, and Towns got a hand on San Antonio's final inbounds pass. That sealed a 29-point comeback win. Towns also took hits from Victor Wembanyama and kept him out of the paint much of the night.
 Towns played a similar part as a freshman at St. Joseph High School in Metuchen, N.J. Senior Quenton DeCosey led the Falcons. Towns manned the high post, where his shooting pulled defenders away from the rim and his passing set up easier looks for DeCosey.
 "Karl really came in and understood, like, 'Hey, I might not be the guy some nights,'" said former St. Joe's guard Jimbo Long to Complex. The Falcons went 29-2 and finished fifth in the state that season. In 2014, Towns, Wade Baldwin IV, and Marques Townes led St. Joe's to the NJSIAA Tournament of Champions title.
 Towns sharpened his game with his father, Karl Towns Sr., a former forward at Monmouth University. In one workout, Towns hit 10 straight 3-pointers from 10 spots. Not one shot touched the rim. St. Joe's coach Dave Turco kept urging him to shoot 3s.
 Towns played AAU ball with Sports U - Team IZOD and faced 15-year-olds when he was only 14, per Complex. He later suited up for the Dominican Republic at the 2012 FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament under John Calipari, his future coach at Kentucky. Born in Edison, N.J., he chose to play for his mother's home country.
 At Kentucky, Towns studied kinesiology for one year. The Wildcats won their first 38 games before losing to Wisconsin in the Final Four. The Minnesota Timberwolves picked him No. 1 overall in 2015, and he stayed nine years. In that time, the team reached the Western Conference Finals for the first time in 20 years.
 In Minnesota, Towns moved to power forward to play next to Rudy Gobert, per Complex. When Chris Finch took over as head coach midway through the 2020-21 season, Towns welcomed him warmly. "He didn't have to call me and welcome me, and be super coachable," Finch said, per the outlet. "He could have just made me prove it to him, but he was probably the guy who welcomed me the most and did whatever we asked him to do."
 Towns paid tribute to his mother, Jacqueline Cruz-Towns, during the Knicks' run. She died in April 2020 from complications of COVID-19, Complex reports. He credited her for helping the Knicks get a stop against Wembanyama in Game 2 of the Finals. James Ziemba, a former St. Joe's forward, said Towns still keeps in touch with his high school friends.
 "He's a champion now," Ziemba said, per Complex. "Karl's vindicated. It vindicates who he is as a person, the way he carries himself, the way he is as a teammate."
